events.title: v0.10.26: Mac Speed and Clearer Clubs
events.summary: Version 0.10.25 slowed the match table badly on Macs, and I wanted that fixed fast. This patch puts the Mac back on its old graphics path, smooths out the opening climb, and gives the club one more redraw. Improved The club is redrawn as a clover, with deep notches between its three leaves and a thin stem, so it is much harder to mistake for a spade, even on the smallest cards where it used to blur into a blob. events.title: v0.10.24: The Mountain and the Count
events.summary: This patch is about how a match feels. A lot of the table used to react before the card or peg that earned it had landed, so I went through the match beat by beat and put every sound and move in order, and the opening is now a climb up the mountain you are about to play. There is also a round of readability fixes so the table reads by light and dark, not only by color. events.title: v0.10.25: Card Legibility
events.summary: Playtest feedback said the hand read small and busy, and that clubs looked a lot like spades. So this release is a pass over the card faces. Added Face cards print their rank a second time on a small plate in the bottom-left corner. When cards overlap on the played row and hide their right side, you can still tell a jack from a queen from a king. events.title: v0.10.23: Lap Gold and House Scores
events.summary: I wanted every lap shop in a weekly challenge to give you a choice. It used to open with an empty purse, so selling your cards back was all you could do there. Added Weekly challenges and practice runs now pay 10 gold each time your peg finishes a lap. Your peg stops at the gate, the gold flies to your purse, and the lap shop opens with something to spend. events.title: v0.10.22: A home for the weekly challenge
events.summary: I measured the ten weekly challenges. For a player who didn't build around the kit, eight leaned hard toward the rival and two leaned hard the other way, so I rebuilt every kit. The challenges were also hard to find and needed the online board to play at all, so they now have their own page and you can practice any of them offline. events.title: Dev diary: how the warm-up teaches cribbage in two hands
events.summary: Cribbage has a reputation for being hard to learn. The rules are easy enough. The hard part is counting your hand. You add up fifteens, pairs, runs and flushes all at once, out loud, while your opponent listens for anything you missed. So I made the warm-up skip the rules talk and deal you a hand. Hand one is the Coach's The Coach plays the first hand with you, one short step at a time.
